Gleuhr Guide — Standardised Training
Framework (draft)
 Oct 27, 2026  ·  @Aman
This is the overview of the Gleuhr Guide's training framework, for your approval. It is for
you and for the branch managers: how every role is trained, how a person is scored, and
who signs them off before they work alone. The eight role modules are separate
documents, linked below. Each one follows the same template described here.
Nothing in this framework is built into the app yet. The lessons, the check questions, the
ratings, the In training / Trained marks and the progress view are all coming with the
Guide.
Why it exists
In your words, on 27 Oct:
"A structured, role-specific training module must be developed for each designation,
including Doctors, Therapists, Front Desk Executives, Accountants, Inventory
Management staff, and Branch Managers (BMs). Each module must cover the
relevant rules, processes, responsibilities, and operational requirements for that role.
The objective is to ensure that every employee is thoroughly trained before
independently handling their responsibilities. A standardised training framework will
reduce operational gaps, repeated follow-ups, and reactive problem-solving."
And on scoring, the same day:
"along with the Clinic CRM training module, please also include the evaluation criteria
for both theoretical and practical assessments, along with the scoring methodology
to assess the trainees' understanding and performance."
The Guide does this in the app itself. Each person learns their own desk from the screens
they really use. Nobody works alone until their BM has watched them do the real tasks.
The eight modules
One module per role. Your list named six designations; on 27 Oct you settled the two that
needed it. "Inventory Management staff" became a cross-desk Stock module for every
clinic desk that uses the CRM's stock. "Accountants" became the clinic Accounts panel.

blocks.title: Page 4
blocks.text:
The BM and Sales Head modules also explain how to rate a team member and how to read
the team's progress, as coming with the Guide.
Evaluation and scoring
Every module is scored the same way. A person passes two parts, and each must pass on
its own. A good score on one never makes up for the other.
Ratings are never averaged. For example, 5, 5, 4, 3, 5 is "not yet": the person repeats only
the task rated 3. There is no list of critical errors (your ruling): no single mistake fails a task
on its own; a mistake lowers that task's rating.
What each rating means (approved by you, 27 Oct):
5: did it alone, right first time, at normal desk speed.
4: did it alone and right, but slower, or caught and fixed their own small slip.
3: needed one prompt, or made one mistake that had to be pointed out.
2: needed several prompts, or made a mistake someone else had to fix.

blocks.title: Page 5
blocks.text:
1: could not do it yet.
What the BM looks at in every task (approved, the same for every module):
1 . Steps. The right steps, in the right order, with nothing skipped.
2. Screen. The right page, buttons and choices; refusals read and acted on.
3. Rules. The module's rules kept: the right person decides, nothing is overwritten, every
visit and call ends with a next step.
4. The patient. Clear and polite, explains what happens next, and hands off to the right
colleague.
5. Pace. Done at normal desk speed, without holding up the patient or the queue.
Each sign-off task in every module also has its own line, "What a 5 looks like", naming the
2–4 things the BM watches for in that task. For example, for reception's first task: finds
her on today's list, checks her in on her booking, records the fee with its transaction ID,
reads her number back, and she lands on the doctor's and counsellor's lists.
Sign-off: In training and Trained
This is coming with the Guide. None of it is built yet.
A new joiner works through the lessons of their module. Every attempt is kept.
When every lesson is passed, their BM watches them do the "Ready for sign-off" tasks
on the real desk and rates each one from 1 to 5.
When every lesson is passed AND every task is rated 4 or 5, the BM signs them off as
Trained.
Until then, their desk shows In training. Nothing is blocked: they can still work, under
the BM's eye.
A BM is signed off by the Sales Head.
The progress view (for the BM and the Sales Head) will show:
for each lesson: the score and every attempt;
for each practical task: every rating, with the BM's name, the date and the BM's one
line;
the result: In training or Trained.
The BM signs off every clinic desk on her team, doctors included. Accounts staff are
signed off by their own sign-off lead. Who signs off a Sales Head is not named in the app.
A proposal for your decision: "What changed" lessons
This is a proposal, not something you have ruled on.

blocks.title: Page 6
blocks.text:
The app changes often. A person trained in October may not know a button that changed
in November. The proposal:
When a change in the app alters how a desk works, the Guide adds a short "What
changed" lesson to that module: one card, and one or two check questions.
A person who is already Trained stays Trained. The new lesson simply shows as due on
their desk and in the BM's progress view.
The BM can see who has not done it yet.
For example: when reception gained Cancel link & collect here on 27 Oct, every Trained
reception person would see one due lesson, "Cancelling a payment link at the desk", with
its two questions.
This keeps training current without sending anyone back to "In training" for every change.
Your open questions, from all eight modules
Each module lists its own questions in its founder section. Here they are in one place.
Each has one example of an answer.
Still open
1 . Is there a set day each week for the counsellor to check No follow-up and Unclosed
visits? For example: every Monday, before the huddle.
2. The counsellor's new follow-up call panel is live only in Chandigarh. The cards
describe the older panel and name the difference once. For example: keep it that way
until every clinic moves, or write a second set of call cards for Chandigarh now.
3. Do you want "What changed" lessons? See the proposal above. For example: yes, one
short lesson per change; a Trained person stays Trained.
Answered on 27 Oct (now in the modules)
Scoring: the 1–5 meanings and the five things the BM watches are approved.
Sign-off: the BM signs off every clinic desk on her team; accounts staff are signed off
by their own sign-off lead; the Sales Head signs off the BM.
Same day: the BM locks each day, and decides each approval, on the day itself. The
Sales Head has no set response time for his own approvals.
Sales Head: Reverse on a waived fee is described as it is today (it does nothing); a
flagged hard-close is final.
Reception: an amendment goes to the Sales Head ("Send to the Sales Head"); a patient
who leaves after check-in is written on her record (Notes → Add a note); no weekly
task.
